# dial

> 48 React components and 452 design tokens. dial-react is not on npm yet. Install the release tarball (pnpm run release:pack writes it to release/): npm install /path/to/release/dial-react-0.0.0.tgz, then import 'dial-react/all.css' once at the root.

## Components

- ActionSheet: ActionSheet is a short lid of actions for one object that rises from the bottom of a phone, the rows printed like Menu's and Cancel a separate plastic key, and on a wide screen it opens as a panel by its key. `import { ActionSheet } from 'dial-react';`
- Badge: Badge is printing on the case of an appliance. It is a small status lamp with its own shape per tone and a word beside it, printed flat on the plastic with no box, no fill, no shadow and never orange; only the lit lamp is a small glass bead in its status hue. `import { Badge } from 'dial-react';`
- Banner: Banner is a strip of the case set into the flow at the top of a screen that says in a printed glyph and a word what condition holds, and stays there until the condition ends. `import { Banner } from 'dial-react';`
- BottomNav: BottomNav prints the phone app's main sections along the bottom edge of the case like the scale under a radio's dial, glyph over word, with one ink index mark under the section you are in. `import { BottomNav } from 'dial-react';`
- Button: Button is a key on the case of an appliance. It is a capsule of the same matte plastic that drops by its height when pressed and returns on the spring, and only the unit's one primary key is dyed orange. `import { Button } from 'dial-react';`
- Card: Card is the case of a small appliance. It is one rounded body of warm matte plastic, lit from the top left, with its content printed and mounted straight on it at an even inset and its wordmark and model printed on the bottom inset line. `import { Card } from 'dial-react';`
- Checkbox: Checkbox is a small square key on the case of an appliance with its function printed beside it. You press it, it drops and springs back, and a tick in printing ink appears on its face to say the option is on. `import { Checkbox } from 'dial-react';`
- Chip: Chip is a small capsule key on the case for filters and quick presets. A selectable chip latches down like an old radio key, turns to frosted glass in the neutral ink range and lights its lamp, a removable chip carries its own round remove key, and none of them is ever orange. `import { Chip } from 'dial-react';`
- Container: Container holds a page of units to a width the eye can scan, with a margin from the page edge that grows with the screen. `import { Container } from 'dial-react';`
- DeviceCard: DeviceCard is one small appliance on the screen, built from anchor A. Its plastic body has the display across the top, one big orange knob or key where the hand goes, plain keys and a grille beside it, a ruler fader across, and the wordmark and model printed on the bottom edge. `import { DeviceCard } from 'dial-react';`
- Dialog: Dialog is a small appliance body that rises in front of the room to ask one question about a device, with plastic keys at the bottom and at most one orange key for the answer that acts. `import { Dialog } from 'dial-react';`
- Display: Display is the one window of a dial unit that says what the device is doing now, recessed into the plastic body, drawn as LCD segments or OLED text, announced politely and never pressed. `import { Display } from 'dial-react';`
- EmptyState: EmptyState is the printing a room or a list shows before it holds anything, with one line that says what is missing, one sentence of what to do, one key, and at most a quiet drawing made of the system's own unlit parts. `import { EmptyState } from 'dial-react';`
- Environment: Environment is one room's air drawn as a small dial appliance: a plastic body whose LCD says the temperature, printed meters under it reading humidity, air quality, carbon dioxide or noise, an optional grille for activity, and the room name and the time of the reading printed at the foot of the case like a wordmark and a model name. `import { Environment } from 'dial-react';`
- ExplainMode: ExplainMode is the SK 4 manual printed on the real screen. One key turns on a how this works mode that prints each part's name and one line of what it does in the free space under it, joined by a thin leader, while every control keeps working and the same key or Escape takes the printing away. `import { Explain, ExplainMode } from 'dial-react';`
- Grid: Grid places whole units on four, eight or twelve columns, so each appliance keeps one fixed place on the screen and its face is never stretched. `import { Grid, GridItem } from 'dial-react';`
- Grille: Grille is the perforated field of a dial unit whose recessed holes are the meter itself. Lit holes in printing ink show a level, activity or signal, and the value is always named for assistive tech. `import { Grille } from 'dial-react';`
- Heading: Heading is the name printed largest on a unit or a page. It uses the same grotesk and grey ink as the rest of the case, and it is louder only by size and by sitting first on the inset line. `import { Heading } from 'dial-react';`
- Icon: Icon is printing on the case made of holes. Every glyph is a pattern of round dots on a seven by seven matrix, the Grille's own field at icon scale, so a symbol reads as part of the same perforated object. `import { iconPath, Icon } from 'dial-react';`
- IconButton: IconButton is the round 44px key of an appliance with a symbol printed on it in place of a word. It is the same matte plastic as Button, it drops by its height when pressed, and only the unit's one primary key is dyed orange. `import { IconButton } from 'dial-react';`
- Input: Input is a window recessed into the appliance's body that takes text. It is a well the full width of its column, the light falls into it from the top left, and its name is printed above on the inset line like the printing on a case. `import { Input } from 'dial-react';`
- Legend: Legend is the printing round a knob that names every position it has. Every choice stays in plain sight, the one in use is lit at full ink in medium weight with one ink index mark, and turning the knob walks the lit word, so nobody opens a menu to learn what the appliance can do. `import { Legend } from 'dial-react';`
- List: List prints rows of devices or tracks on one plastic body, the way an appliance prints its programmes on the case, with a glyph or a printed index, a name, the state in words and at most one part to work at the end of the row. `import { List, ListItem } from 'dial-react';`
- MediaPlayer: MediaPlayer is the small MP3 player of the reference sheet drawn on a screen, one plastic body with an OLED window that says what is playing and how, the tape fader under it, three round transport keys of which only play is orange, the level in recessed holes and a volume fader, and it really plays the audio it names. `import { MediaPlayer } from 'dial-react';`
- Menu: Menu is a key that opens the same plastic panel as Select, holding a few actions printed in ink as words with a glyph; the one that removes something carries the critical lamp shape beside its word, never a colour. `import { Menu } from 'dial-react';`
- Meter: Meter is a printed scale in a narrow recess with one ink needle, like the tuning scale on a radio, that reads a level the person does not set, such as a battery, the air or the water hardness, and names its region with a glyph and a word, never by colour and never in orange. `import { Meter } from 'dial-react';`
- Progress: Progress shows how far a device task has run, like a washer's cycle or a firmware update, as a recessed groove in the body that fills with printing ink, with its name and reading printed above, and it never moves while idle. `import { Progress } from 'dial-react';`
- PullToRefresh: PullToRefresh is the one-detent fader of a dial list. Pulling the list down at its top drags a printed ink index down a short ruler into its detent; released there, the list settles on the material's spring, holds a still Working reading while the hub answers, and prints the time of the new readings. A round refresh key in the bar does the same without the gesture. `import { PullToRefresh } from 'dial-react';`
- Queue: Queue is the up-next list of a dial player printed on one plastic body like List. Each track is a row with its number in tabular figures, its title, artist and length, the playing row marked by an ink index mark and the word Playing, and every row can be moved or removed from the keyboard as well as by its printed handle. `import { Queue } from 'dial-react';`
- RangeSlider: RangeSlider is Slider with two frosted glass caps in the same ruler groove, setting a low and a high end such as a heating schedule's band or a lamp's warm to cool range; the ruler between the caps is printed in heavier ink and the groove there is lit in the caps' quiet tint, while no part turns orange. `import { RangeSlider } from 'dial-react';`
- Rotary: Rotary is the knob of the appliance. It is a flat disc with one printed index mark over a ring of detent ticks across 270 degrees, dyed orange as the unit's one loud part, and it turns with the hand and settles into the nearest detent on the material's spring. `import { ROTARY_DIAMETER, Rotary } from 'dial-react';`
- SceneCard: SceneCard is a scene of the home, such as Movie night or Good night, printed on a small card of light stock that the person picks up and inserts into a room's Slot. The card is printing on a flat card one step lighter than the plastic, with the name on its top edge so it stays readable when the card stands half out of a slot, and it is never orange. `import { SceneCard } from 'dial-react';`
- Scrubber: Scrubber is the position of a track or a video on a dial player, a frosted glass cap riding the fader groove like the tape position on a deck, the played stretch lit in its quiet tint, with chapter marks printed above, the buffered stretch drawn as a thin ink line along the groove floor and the elapsed and remaining time printed in tabular figures under its ends, while the orange stays on the play key. `import { formatTime, Scrubber } from 'dial-react';`
- SegmentedControl: SegmentedControl is the bank of band keys on the case of a radio (FM, AM, AUX). The keys interlock, pressing one latches it down as a frosted glass key in the neutral ink range with its lamp lit, and the key that was down springs back up in matte plastic. `import { SegmentedControl } from 'dial-react';`
- Select: Select is the same recessed window as Input with a printed chevron, and it opens a plastic panel of options above the page; the chosen option is marked by a printed tick and weight, the way a selector on an appliance marks its setting in ink. `import { Select } from 'dial-react';`
- Sheet: Sheet is the lid of an appliance opened to show every control of one device at once, rising from the bottom edge of a phone and standing as its own unit at the lower end of a wide screen. `import { Sheet } from 'dial-react';`
- Skeleton: Skeleton is the dial unit with its power off. The window shows ghost segments, the grille shows unlit holes, keys and text lines are flat plastic of their own size, and nothing moves until the content arrives. `import { Skeleton } from 'dial-react';`
- Slider: Slider is the fader on the face of an appliance. A frosted glass cap, tinted in the value's own range, rides a recessed groove under a printed ruler scale, the groove behind it lit in the same tint, follows the hand and settles into the nearest detent on the material's spring, while the orange stays on the unit's rotary. `import { Slider } from 'dial-react';`
- Slot: Slot is the narrow mouth a room or a device unit has for a scene card. It is a recessed slit in the plastic with the room's name printed under it and a lamp beside it. Inserting a SceneCard runs the scene, the card then stands half out of the slit with its name readable, and the lamp lights with a word. `import { Slot } from 'dial-react';`
- Snackbar: Snackbar is Toast's strip of matte plastic placed once, centred just above the phone's bottom nav, saying what just happened with a printed glyph and word and offering one key that undoes it. `import { SnackbarProvider, useSnackbar, Snackbar } from 'dial-react';`
- Stack: Stack lines up units and parts on the 4px step, so the gaps between appliances on a screen follow the same rhythm as the holes and insets inside them. `import { Stack } from 'dial-react';`
- Switch: Switch is the slide switch on the side of an appliance. A plastic cap slides in a recessed groove between two printed positions, and a small lamp beside it is lit as a glass bead in the neutral ink range while it is on. `import { Switch } from 'dial-react';`
- Tabs: Tabs are the section names printed along the case of an appliance, like the scale under a selector. The chosen room's name is set in medium weight with one ink index mark under it, and the screen below shows that room. `import { Tabs } from 'dial-react';`
- Text: Text is the printing on the case of an appliance. It is one grotesk in two weights, grey ink flat on the plastic, with hierarchy told by size and by where the words sit on the unit. `import { Text } from 'dial-react';`
- TimePicker: TimePicker is the set window of a clock radio, a recessed well that holds the hour and minute as ink figures, each a field that steps like a detent, with a pair of round set keys under each field and no orange, because a time is a setting and not the unit's loud control. `import { TimePicker } from 'dial-react';`
- Toast: Toast is a short strip of plastic that rises at the bottom of the screen after an action and says in a printed glyph and a word what the device just did, then goes away. `import { ToastProvider, useToast, Toast } from 'dial-react';`
- Tray: Tray is a recess pressed into a dial unit that gathers its small secondary keys, such as previous, next, a mode key and a lamp, into one place. With the small keys sunk together in one tray, the unit's one big orange part stands alone on the plastic, the way a recessed key tray sits beside the main knob of a synthesiser. `import { Tray } from 'dial-react';`
- Wiring: Wiring prints the relations between parts on the face itself, the way a schematic pedal face joins a knob to the circuit it shapes. It draws a printed box around a group of parts, hairlines of ink with one bend at most joining them, and one short lowercase word on a line, so a person sees that the thermostat sets the heater before touching anything. `import { WiringNode, WiringGroup, Wiring } from 'dial-react';`
